items.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022
items.q: I’ve worked with Lou Adler a lot because of Tom Scott and Gene McDaniels, Merrick Clayton

ctx.x: Yeah, they could see if it was literally being played correctly.

I’ll tell you guys would surprise me sometimes. I’ve worked with Lou Adler a lot because of Tom Scott and Gene McDaniels, Merrick Clayton, you know he had a nice roster of acts and Lou would always make sure that the artists were comfortable. I mean if we got out one tune a day he was happy with that. Then you had the other producers that were working for — like the company kind of guys you know, guys like RCA, stiff as they were, I mean they had to get three tunes a day, blah-blah-blah-blah. Everything had to be…

And artists a lot of times, especially the solo singers, they may be coming in and hearing this orchestration for the first time. They may have sat with a piano player and gone through arrangements but then if you have a whole string section or a big band it must take time for the art sort of to adjust themselves to that.
